ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Drunk driving can lead to many safety hazards, one of which is that the driver's reaction time becomes longer. "Reaction time" refers to the time from when the driver discovers the situation to when the driver begins to take braking action. In the table below, "reaction distance" refers to the distance traveled by the car during the time from when the driver discovers the situation to when the driver takes braking action; "braking distance" refers to the distance traveled by the car during the time from when the driver steps on the brake pedal to brake to when the car stops. By analyzing the above table, it can be known that which of the following statements is correct
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When the car brakes, the magnitude of the acceleration is $7.5\mathrm{m/s}^2$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: By analyzing the above table, what is the magnitude of the acceleration when the car brakes?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When the car brakes, the magnitude of the acceleration is $7.5\mathrm{m/s}^2$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the image there is a table, the left side is "speed", and the speed given in this row is 15 m/s; the table also lists "reaction distance" and "braking distance", among which the "braking distance" is 15 m under both the normal and drunk columns. Then reason: the initial speed when the car starts braking is v0=15 m/s, the final speed when braking to a stop is v=0, and the displacement during the braking process is s=15 m. Substitute into the uniformly accelerated linear motion formula v²-v0²=2as, obtaining 0²-15²=2a×15, so -225=30a, a=-7.5 m/s². The negative sign indicates that the acceleration direction is opposite to the direction of motion, therefore the magnitude of the acceleration when braking is 7.5 m/s².
